statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail eases further because the overnight Iran-strike range has now held unchanged for a full hour with price mid-range and both extremes rejected, while Stress stays elevated on an oil, geopolitical, rate-path and month-end catalyst stack.
recommendation: Conditions are described as two-way inside an unchanged roughly 270-point overnight range against an elevated event backdrop. A narrow evidence-based danger window is flagged from 13:30 to 16:00 UTC around the U.S. cash open and the 14:30 UTC Dallas Fed release, where the mapped state moves to WATCH.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures hold an unchanged 270-point overnight range near 29,460 as Brent steadies above $91 after renewed US-Iran strikes
body: U.S. forces struck Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island near the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday, disrupting an attempted mining operation, and Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they targeted U.S. bases in Jordan and the United Arab Emirates in retaliation, with the missiles intercepted. Kharg Island, which handles roughly 90% of Iran's crude exports, has been publicly threatened, and the U.S. Treasury has flagged weekly secondary sanctions on Iran's trading partners. Brent trades near $91.12, up about 3.4%, with WTI near $86.53, up about 3.8%; both have eased marginally from the highs seen an hour earlier rather than extending. Nasdaq-100 futures fell to 29,274.75 on the overnight headlines, fully retraced, extended to 29,545.50, and now trade near 29,458.50, down 0.11%. That 29,274.75-29,545.50 range is unchanged over the past hour, neither extreme has been retested, and price sits mid-range. S&P 500 futures are near 7,709.50, down 0.16%, inside a 7,684.25-7,724.00 range. The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed Friday at 29,433.43 after a 0.70% decline, with the 10-year Treasury yield up 4.8 basis points to 4.72% and the 2-year up about 8 basis points. VIX is 15.22 with a 15.16-15.28 day range, up 5.5% from Friday's 14.43 close but still low in absolute terms. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole remarks lifted September rate-hike odds to roughly 57.5% from about 35.4% beforehand. The decisive observation for this assessment is that an additional full hour has passed without either range extreme being retested, which is direct evidence that mean reversion is functioning; amplifier count remains high while observed price-path structure stays two-sided. Today is the last trading session of August, so month-end rebalancing is an additional mechanical factor into the 20:00 UTC close. Shared Finviz cross-asset context was about 226 minutes old at assessment time and was therefore treated as stale under the inherited freshness rule and used for discovery only, with all levels above taken from independent primary-source research.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly Claude assessments were available and every one mapped to EA_ON. Tail held at 5 through the Sunday reopen window, rose to a peak of 15 at 00:00 UTC as the Iran escalation was first priced, decayed back to 5 by 07:00-08:00 UTC, then jumped to 17 at 09:00 UTC as oil extended, before easing to 11 at 10:00 UTC. Stress climbed from 26 to a peak of 52. Dominant mode moved from normal to mixed after 23:00 UTC, with one trend-down hour at 00:00 UTC and event/whipsaw at 09:00 and 10:00 UTC. The pattern is an event shock that was absorbed rather than extended.
outlookSummary: The 24-hour outlook keeps the mapped state at EA_ON for 22 of 24 hours. Conditional Tail runs 10-11 through the European afternoon, is raised to 17 into the cash-open approach and to 21 and 20 for the two hours inside the flagged 13:30-16:00 UTC danger window, where the mapped state becomes WATCH. It steps down to 13-16 through the U.S. afternoon, rises to 17 into the 20:00 UTC month-end close, then settles to a 9-12 overnight baseline across the Asian and European sessions, drifting up at the end of the horizon as the September 1 ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS block at 14:00 UTC approaches from outside it. Stress peaks near 57 around the cash open and decays toward 40-46 overnight. Confidence declines from 87 to 60 with horizon.

Both extremes were rejected and neither has been retested, so mean reversion is holding. Tail eases while Stress stays elevated on the oil and rate-path stack.
